records.title: E4 Stockholm bypass and the staged opening
records.answer: A predominantly tunnelled road is approaching a partial opening. The useful distinction is between a northern link, the eventual through-route and the operating evidence needed to judge either.
records.scope: One E4 Förbifart Stockholm project between Kungens kurva and Häggvik, counted once across tunnel sections, interchanges and opening stages. It is not the whole E4, the wider Stockholm road network or a separate project for each tunnel.
records.stage: Construction and pre-opening preparation documented; December 6, 2026 partial opening and 2030 full opening remain scheduled rather than observed

historical_acquisition.decision: Additive named account for the retained historical acquisition docket; original identity fields and stage tests remain unchanged

identity_decision.rationale: The authority identifies one bounded E4 alignment with connected tunnel and interchange components. Different construction contracts and opening stages do not create additional projects. Its regional corridor is distinct from Slussen redevelopment and from Stockholm municipality, so this adds one project identity without admitting whole-route operation.

timeline.event: The northern-tunnel engineering description documented groundwater and sealing issues for an application; this is a document date, not a current permit decision.
Trafikverket announced a December 6 partial-opening schedule, keeping the whole-route forecast at 2030.
Trafikverket published its account of an emergency exercise held earlier in the autumn.

sections.heading: A regional link built mainly underground
sections.text: The bypass follows a 21-kilometre alignment west of Stockholm, with more than 18 kilometres in tunnels and six interchanges. Its endpoints are Kungens kurva and Häggvik. Putting most of the road underground changes the delivery problem: excavation must be followed by roads, power, ventilation, communications and traffic control before the tunnel can function as a transport service. The alignment also reaches beyond a single municipal place account. A regional road project should therefore be evaluated against its own corridor and connecting network, rather than treating every change in Stockholm traffic as an effect of the bypass.

sections.heading: The first opening covers only the northern section
sections.text: The October 7 announcement schedules approximately 3.5 kilometres between Häggvik and Hjulsta to open on December 6, 2026. About 1.8 kilometres of that section runs in tunnel. Work continues on the longer connection toward Kungens kurva, with the full route forecast for 2030. As of this November 22 review, the first opening remains future-dated. The partial route can change access and traffic distribution before the eventual through-route exists, so early results will need to identify exactly which roads were available. The forecast end-to-end journey time is not an observed operating result.

sections.heading: The interim traffic arrangement is not symmetrical
sections.text: The November 13 description gives the northern section three lanes northbound, while southbound traffic progressively narrows before leaving at Hjulsta. The authority also describes a reduction in the southbound speed setting as vehicles approach that exit. These are features of an interim connection, not a statement that the full bypass will operate as a one-lane road. They matter when interpreting the first traffic counts: a constraint near the temporary end of the route may influence queues and route choice even when the underground link itself is functioning. Opening-stage geometry belongs beside any later comparison.

sections.heading: An exercise tests coordination before normal traffic
sections.text: Trafikverket’s November 10 account describes two emergency scenarios in the Akalla and Hästa tunnels earlier that autumn. Emergency services, traffic operators and alarm centres practised together, with actors representing casualties. The authority reports positive observer feedback, while also describing the collection of lessons for further work. This is evidence of preparation in the actual facility, not a public-service reliability series or a separately retrieved opening authorization. It illustrates the organizational side of tunnel operation: technical systems need people who can coordinate traffic, access and assistance when an incident interrupts normal travel.

sections.heading: Groundwater constraints have their own history
sections.text: A technical description dated April 23, 2021 explains that parts of the northern tunnels encountered more fractured and water-bearing rock than expected. It supports an application for greater groundwater diversion and protective infiltration along specified sections. Sealing the rock and maintaining surrounding groundwater are related engineering tasks, but they are not interchangeable with road-opening tests. This historical submission does not establish the present court disposition or measured conditions in 2026. Nor does its conditional discussion of a later completion date replace the authority’s current schedule. Follow-up needs the applicable decision and subsequent monitoring for the same sections.

sections.heading: Measure access and disruption across the connected network
sections.text: Once a section actually opens, a useful account would compare travel-time variability, incident recovery, bus access and traffic distribution over defined operating periods. Counts should identify direction, location, season and the available network, including construction elsewhere. Environmental comparisons need their own exposure and emissions boundaries rather than assuming that moving traffic underground eliminates its effects. The key public question is how the link changes access and resilience for people and freight, including those who do not drive through it. That requires repeated observations, not a capacity headline or a single ceremonial opening.

next_artifacts: A dated actual-opening and accepted-configuration record for the Häggvik–Hjulsta section.
Comparable traffic, disruption and access observations for the partial network, followed separately by whole-route observations.
The applicable groundwater disposition and subsequent monitoring for the sections discussed in the 2021 submission.

records.title: Slussen redevelopment and staged handovers
records.answer: Slussen combines transport interchange, public space and water regulation. Some spaces have opened, while terminal readiness and waterworks adjustments continue on separate tracks.
records.scope: One integrated Slussen redevelopment at the meeting of Södermalm, Gamla stan, Mälaren and Saltsjön. The bus terminal, bridges, public spaces and water-control works are components, not separately counted projects. The municipality and wider lake catchment are not this project’s identity.
records.stage: Several public-space milestones completed and bus terminal transferred; passenger service and full waterworks acceptance are not established by those milestones

historical_acquisition.decision: Additive named account for the retained historical acquisition docket; original identity fields and stage tests remain unchanged

identity_decision.rationale: Stockholm presents Slussen as an integrated replacement and redevelopment with connected transport, public-space and water functions. Those components remain one project despite different owners, contracts and readiness dates. This is distinct from the E4 bypass and the municipal place account; no separate terminal, bridge or district is counted here.

timeline.event: Slussbron opened, according to the municipal completed-milestone account.
Vattentorget and adjoining named public-space connections opened.
Region Stockholm took over the new bus terminal; handover is distinct from passenger traffic starting.
The worksite body’s update label accompanies continuing erosion-protection adjustments; the separate footer retains October 16.

sections.heading: Replacement joins transport and water functions
sections.text: The city describes Slussen as worn-out infrastructure requiring replacement, while retaining its role as an interchange between different ways of travelling. Redevelopment also changes public space and the ability to release water from Mälaren toward the Baltic. These functions share a constrained location but serve different users and operating conditions. The transport terminal can be ready for one type of handover while water-control works still need adjustment. Treating the redevelopment as a single ribbon-cutting event would obscure the sequence through which each function becomes usable and the different organizations responsible for operating it.

sections.heading: Opened spaces establish a partial service history
sections.text: The municipal milestone account records Slussbron opening in October 2020 and Vattentorget opening on June 6, 2024, together with adjoining pedestrian and cycling connections. These are concrete parts of the area that people can use while construction continues elsewhere. Their completion does not establish that every promised connection, commercial space or landscaped area is finished. A useful public-space account follows the routes people can actually take between destinations, including temporary diversions and changes in access. That distinguishes the opening of a particular space from completion of the surrounding interchange.

sections.heading: Water tests led to additional protection work
sections.text: The construction page’s November 16 body update says tests identified a need to strengthen erosion protection in the discharge channels. Concrete works are planned through March 2027, and the lock’s boat opening remains conditional on the pedestrian-and-cycle bridge being finished and the water area no longer being a worksite. The page separately retains an October 16 footer date. The later operational detail is more informative than a broad annual completion forecast. It records a specific adjustment still being made, not full waterworks acceptance or a measured reduction in flood losses across the lake region.

sections.heading: Terminal handover is not the start of passenger service
sections.text: Region Stockholm took over the Katarinaberget bus terminal on September 30, 2026. Its November 13 readiness update still gave no fixed date for passenger traffic, explaining that technical and traffic tests must be evaluated before an opening can be announced. The two statements describe different transitions: transfer between organizations and entry into service. Until the passenger move occurs, temporary stopping arrangements continue to shape journeys. An opening account should therefore identify which lines move, how passengers reach the new waiting areas and connections, and what remains outside the new terminal.

sections.heading: Training and exercises reveal the remaining preparation
sections.text: The week 47 update reports that more than 75 percent of drivers had completed training and describes a double-decker recovery test. It also records a fire exercise without actors representing passengers, with a larger exercise planned for December 8. These details make readiness more concrete than a general statement that work is progressing. They do not convert the planned exercise into an opening date or demonstrate passenger handling under every condition. The report exposes only relative publication labels, so its exact publication day is left unspecified rather than reconstructed from a changing label.

sections.heading: Follow the completed passenger and water journeys
sections.text: The next account should trace a passenger from the temporary arrangement into the permanent interchange, including walking distance, step-free access, information, transfers and service interruptions. Water operations need a different record: completed adjustments, accepted operating arrangements and performance during defined conditions. A good redevelopment can improve both functions, but evidence for one cannot stand in for the other. The project’s public value also depends on how construction burdens and eventual benefits are distributed around the site. Keeping those journeys and responsibilities visible is more useful than adding together unrelated completion percentages.

next_artifacts: A dated passenger-service start and line-by-line terminal move, distinct from the September 30 handover.
Completed waterworks adjustments and accepted operating arrangements, followed by observations under stated conditions.
Post-opening accessibility, transfer and public-space observations that identify which routes and components were available.

records.title: Stockholm municipal services and environmental responsibilities
records.answer: Stockholm’s municipal account connects district services, environmental goals, water delivery and resident feedback without turning a regional project or one sampling result into a citywide score.
records.scope: One Stockholm municipality, also called Stockholms stad or Stockholms kommun. It is not Stockholm County, the metropolitan region, the whole water-utility service area or a separate place for each district. District changes are retained within one municipal identity.
records.stage: Municipal geography, service responsibilities and dated programme and sampling records established; citywide achievement and project-caused outcomes are not inferred

historical_acquisition.decision: Additive named account for the retained historical acquisition docket; original identity fields and stage tests remain unchanged

identity_decision.rationale: The city’s own geography and district-governance accounts define one municipality with internal administrative divisions. The regional transport authority, water service geography and project footprints have different boundaries. Counting one municipality preserves those distinctions and does not turn eleven districts or the two featured projects into additional places.

timeline.event: District mergers formed Järva and Norra innerstaden within the existing municipality.
The city council adopted Environment Programme 2030, according to the municipal programme account.
The utility dated its north-west point-of-use report for 2025 sampling; this is not a 2026 sampling period.
The resident-survey page was updated with the 2026 city and district publication structure.

sections.heading: One municipality contains different service areas
sections.text: Stockholm’s geography page identifies eleven district areas, including Järva and Norra innerstaden formed through internal mergers on July 1, 2023. Those changes do not create new municipalities. District boards make decisions on services such as municipal preschool, elder care, disability support and local public space. A citywide comparison should retain that internal geography when assessing access and service demand. It should also distinguish municipal responsibilities from the regional transport authority and from utility networks that serve people across administrative borders. Otherwise a large project can appear to solve a local service problem simply because both carry the Stockholm name.

sections.heading: Environmental goals define work rather than certify success
sections.text: The city council adopted Environment Programme 2030 on September 23, 2024. Its account connects lower climate impact with adaptation, ecosystems, resource use, cleaner environments and a fair transition. The programme distinguishes the city’s own organization from the wider activities of residents and businesses, which matters when assigning responsibility for action. A municipal target is a direction for work, not evidence that the target has been reached. Progress should be attached to the relevant geography, baseline and reporting period, while the distribution of exposure and access remains visible across different neighbourhoods.

sections.heading: Drinking water has a chain of controls
sections.text: Stockholm Vatten och Avfall describes checks from raw water in Mälaren through treatment at Lovö and Norsborg, onward through the distribution system and at users’ premises. The control points answer different questions: conditions at a treatment plant are not identical to those at the end of a distribution route. This makes water service a relationship between source protection, treatment, pipes and receiving buildings. A complete municipal account needs both quality and continuity, with interruptions and repairs linked to the areas affected. The existence of a sampling programme alone does not establish continuous service at every tap.

sections.heading: Annual averages retain their sampling boundary
sections.text: The north-west point-of-use report is dated March 30, 2026 but describes sampling in 2025. It reports annual mean values, including total hardness of 5.6 degrees dH. That is neither a maximum nor a current reading at a particular household. Its footnotes describe the sampling programme and the meaning of values below quantification limits; programme counts should not be assigned entirely to the north-west area without a clear geographic breakdown. The report is useful as a bounded service observation, not as a health assurance, a citywide compliance verdict or evidence of uninterrupted supply.

sections.heading: Resident feedback answers another part of the question
sections.text: The city’s annual resident-survey explanation describes randomly selected residents answering questions about service and the urban environment, with 2026 publications organized at city and district levels. This identifies a route for understanding how people experience services alongside technical records. The publication page does not itself establish the survey’s numerical results, response rate or a causal effect of a project. A future comparison should inspect those reports and their methods before combining them with operational data. Satisfaction, measured service performance and exposure to construction can each reveal something important without being interchangeable measures.

sections.heading: Join projects to everyday access without merging their boundaries
sections.text: The bypass and Slussen illuminate different municipal interfaces. One is a regional road connection approaching a partial opening; the other combines a central interchange, public space and water-control functions with separate readiness stages. A stronger place account would follow how residents reach work, education and services as those arrangements change, rather than assigning every regional benefit to the municipality. It would also examine which neighbourhoods bear disruption and which gain practical access. Maintaining stable places, service responsibilities and observation periods makes those comparisons possible without inventing a single score for the city.

next_artifacts: District-level service and access observations with stable geography and explicit reporting periods.
The actual 2026 resident-survey reports and methods before quoting results or linking perceptions to projects.
Comparable quality and interruption records for defined water-service areas, alongside dated environmental-programme results.
